media-press.quote: Statement from David McCraw, Senior Vice President and Deputy General Counsel at the New York Times:

ai-technology.quote:
Ethics enforcement would be left to a DOJ that has shown no appetite for reining in Trump’s corruption. The provision would expire in 2029, and explicitly bars retroactive enforcement against Trump.

Any fine is capped at $500k: less than 0.04% of what the President brought in from crypto last year.

Sen. Elizabeth Warren previously raised concerns about corruption at the OCC after a memo from Palmer Luckey’s Erebor neo-bank promised investors they could secure a charter in a whirlwind six months thanks to “unique connectivity to banking regulators” and “Palmer’s political network”.

The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency has granted final approval to USDC stablecoin issuer Circle to operate as a national trust bank. Comptroller Jonathan Gould previously represented Circle as a client when he was a partner at Jones Day.

The Department of Justice is reportedly planning to drop charges against Matthew Goettsche, who ran a crypto Ponzi scheme that bilked $722 million from investors he described as “dumb” and “sheep”, after he hired Trump-linked lawyers to lobby for legal relief.

Though Trump supposedly said it was a “disgrace” that a teleprompter operator was using inside access to his speeches to profit from Kalshi bets, Trump’s Truth Social is now planning to monetize the same type of early access to the President’s statements.
